130	### Core Rules
131	
132	Rule ids are `HE-n`; formulas `HE-F n` (Formulas section, ids reserved in the index at the end of this section); edge cases `E-HE-n`; acceptance criteria `AC-HE-n`; conflicts `C-HE-n`. Every Horror-owned number is `[PLACEHOLDER]` and a registry candidate unless marked CITED (a locked name quoted verbatim with its registry value) or DERIVED. The Graph's `RUPTURE_HP`, `BREACH_HP`, `FOOTPRINT_MAX_Q`, `FOOTPRINT_MAX_GOUGE_BP`, `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS` and `C_TILE` are Life-Support Graph registry constants (registered 2026-10-27), cited with the registry value and their LSG line and never restated as Horror's own. Rules state observable behaviour and contracts; implementation patterns are marked "-> ADR candidate". "Run" means one execution of the `horror.step` hook (every 5th tick).
133	
134	#### Group A — Identity, scope and ownership
135	
136	**HE-1. One type, one instance, one behaviour cycle.** *Rule.* MVP ships exactly one type row, `horror_t01` (a placeholder name, renamed never aliased: floor-attached, three-branch, about 1.5 times crewmate height, one extensible reach limb; the art bible's outer-ring working target, ART:546), at most `HORROR_MAX_MVP` 1 resident record, and one behaviour cycle: **LURK (CALM) / STALK (TELL) → REACH (telegraph) → STRIKE → RETREAT**, plus `TRANSIT` while it passes through a hull. The motion vocabulary of the art matrix maps onto it as *creep* (LURK, STALK, RETREAT), *unfold* (REACH) and *snap* (STRIKE). "One behaviour" is **one cycle of one type, never three monsters.** More types, per-ring rosters, filament-riders, hidden-entity wiring, `repel`, flares and decoys, and co-op replication are Vertical Slice and are named in Open Questions and in the block shape only. *Why.* The concept's MVP item 4 is "Attention with one threshold and one horror behaviour"; AT-11 makes a told breach without teeth a named design failure (cry-wolf; commit dominates abort), and the art bible names the reach as the signature image (ART 5.4). *Cites.* AT:197, AT:373, CON MVP definition, ART:546.
137	
138	**HE-2. A real horror is a true SIM entity that touches nothing optical.** *Rule.* A horror has a true integer position in its own block, is solid to Layout solids and to nothing else (it passes through crewmates and they through it, BDY-17), is drawn in the single Y-sorted layer so its sprite hides what stands behind it, is hidden by walls and by darkness, and is revealed only by light. It **contributes no occluder, casts no shadow, emits nothing, and never changes the beam, any subject's `lux`, `lit` or any emitter field.** "Real occlusion" in the index row and the routed thread is read as *visual opacity by draw order plus locomotion against Layout solids*, never as a `LightOccluder2D`. Nothing a horror does is a light event except the disturbance state of HE-35, which Lighting reads and executes. *Why.* Three designed GDDs decide it (EM-20 (c) and AC-24; Lighting rail 10 "Horrors cast no shadow and emit nothing" and AC-LO-16; Failure & Trail FT-31) and the art bible's own recommendation agrees (ART:296); a horror shadow would destroy the free stage-2 sanity falsifier "a shadow with no occluder" and with it Pillar 4's "no lie is unfalsifiable". "Displace dust" from the art bible is retained in spirit through the marks of HE-30, not through the Attention Presenter's shared dust process. *(orchestrator ruling: option A, affirmed by the creative-director at the CD-GDD-ALIGN gate as R1; the fiction gloss "the web does not stop light; it only takes it" is adopted; the wording refreshes are owed rows, never edits here.)* **Gate.** Until the owed ART:542, ART 5.5, PIPE:140 and IDX:35 refresh rows land, the art bible and this GDD contradict each other; those rows are a BLOCKING precondition of `/asset-spec` for the rig (AC-HE-123), as C-HE-21 is for rime. *Cites.* EM:208, LO:151, FT:199, ART:296, ART:542.
139	
140	**HE-3. Block and hook identity.** *Rule.* Block `horror.state`: class `SIM`, `persist` true, `persist_scope` WORLD, scope SHARED, `repl_hint` SHARED_SUMMARY, `schema_version` 1, `supported_versions` [1], `restore_after` `[layout.state, graph.state, emitter.state, attention.state]`. Hook `horror.step`: divisor 5, offset 0, `after: [attention.step, emitter.place]` (the must-repeats of Attention (AT:373), the Emitter (EM AC-60) and the kernel (KRN:201), exactly as ruled; C-HE-20 closed). A hook id that is unknown at boot fails boot (CR-3, no alias concept); grep of `horror.step`, `horror.state` and `horror.view` across the neighbours before closing found no collision. The read view is `horror.view` (HE-37). *Why.* `body.integrate` precedes `horror.step` on every Horror tick through `emitter.place`'s own `after` list (EM:104: `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]`) and the CR-3 total order, so the same-tick seat read that the exact walk-out arithmetic of HE-F2 needs holds without extending the ruled list; Horror writes nothing Body reads, so no cycle can form. A one-tick-stale seat read would let an escaping seat read up to 2 px closer than it is. *Cites.* KRN:71, KRN:201, EM:104, AT:125-131, BDY-8.
141	
142	**HE-4. Cadence: one run is one rig pose, and what Horror reads between Attention's runs.** *Rule.* `horror.step` runs on ticks that are multiples of 5 (12 Hz), so one run is exactly one 12 fps rig pose (PIPE row 14). Attention and the Graph run at divisor 6; LCM(5, 6) = 30, so the two hooks coincide only when `T mod 30 = 0`, and CR-3's `after` orders the pair only on those ticks. On every other run Horror reads `attention.view` **as committed by Attention's most recent run**; this is a reading of committed state, not a new kernel rule. Presentation interpolates `pos_prev` to `pos_curr` across the five ticks of a run; the rig pose is stepped, never tweened. Every Horror duration is authored as an integer count of runs and published in ticks as `runs × 5` (`HORROR_RUN_TICKS` 5, DERIVED from the divisor); a duration that is not a multiple of 5 is a data-load lint failure (it would silently round up to the next run, a 1 to 4 tick bias that matters at the `UNFOLD_LO` bound). **The lint covers every SIM-clock duration** (`UNFOLD_LO`, `UNFOLD_HI`, `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS`, `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS`, `RETURN_DELAY_TICKS`, `LURK_DWELL_TICKS` and the rest of the type row); it **exempts the L3 disturbance lengths `L3_DUR_LO` and `L3_DUR_HI`** (18 and 30), which are published to Lighting in ticks and are presentation-timed (LO-19, the gutter grammar), not run-quantised: a disturbance *starts* on a run, its length does not round to one (C-HE-29). *Cites.* PIPE:303, KRN:71, HE-F5.
143	
144	**HE-5. Data-driven type row.** *Rule.* Every per-type value lives in a data file keyed by `type_id`; behaviour code is generic over the row and contains no behavioural constant. A row carries: `v_creep_mpx`, `v_hunt_mpx`, `r_snap_px`, `reach_range_px`, `hull_contact_px`, `strike_bp`, `strike_cooldown_ticks`, `strike_hold_runs`, `unfold_lo`, `unfold_hi`, `lurk_standoff_px`, `lurk_dwell_ticks`, the L3 constants, the mark and rig asset ids. The data lint refuses any field named `damage`, `accuracy`, `armour`, `dps`, `xp`, `unlock`, `health`, `hp`, `kill`, `loot`, `threat`, `aggro` or `hate` (Horror's own harm field is `strike_bp`, a Suit-scale amount, never `damage`). *Why.* Coding standards (gameplay values are data-driven) and the Item DB's lint AP-2; the field list is also the anti-combat guard (HE-38). *Cites.* IDB:97.
145	
146	**HE-6. Boundaries.** *Rule.* Horror does not read or write Attention's level, does not call `set_beacon`, does not schedule a breach, does not add a Graph footprint kind, does not read any `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, does not move, push or stagger a player (the stagger is the Controller's response to the Suit rung), places no content, narrates nothing, calls no physics query, owns no sound, mix or cue name, owns no HUD element, and holds no stimulus tracker, accumulator, "awareness", "alert", "threat" or "aggro" value, persisted or derived. *Why.* Guard rail 1: absorbing Attention is the most likely way this GDD drifts; the grep of this document for those words outside a negation returns zero (Acceptance Criteria lint).
147	
148	#### Group B — Permission, tell composition and the audit
149	
150	**HE-7. Phase-sourced behaviour, no stored drive.** *Rule.* Every transition between LURK and STALK, and every harm gate, is a function of `attention.view` fields only: `phase`, `tell_epoch`, `tell_outcome`, `locus_section_id`, `exogenous_permitted(section)`, `breach_enter_T`, `phase_enter_T`. The target (HE-13) is recomputed from physical `lux` on every run and is **not persisted**. The only things the record remembers are where it is, what state it is in since when, what it has already done this `tell_epoch` (counts), the locked point of a REACH in flight, and the stream counter. **Debug surface** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: a lethal AI cannot be playtested blind)*: each run also publishes a **non-persisted, non-hashed record `horror.view.debug`** on Horror's registered diagnostics channel (Debug Overlay DO-12, dev builds only), holding the current target ref or ANCHOR with each candidate's `lux_pm`, the goal room and the surrogate goal, the next hop, the transition guard that fired (1 to 7) and the HE-14 condition (a) to (f) that failed last, `hold_runs`, `blocked_runs`, `horror_wedged`, and the `linked` and `connected` results for the nearest seat *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. It is derived from the run, never read back: **no SIM rule, guard, formula or hash input may read `horror.view.debug`** (a lint, AC-HE-135), it is absent from `horror.state`, and it is never an accessibility or player surface (UI Requirements). *Why.* AT-2 (one level for the world), Pillar 1 (no hidden stat), guard rail 1. *Cites.* AT:139, AT:214-232.
151	
152	**HE-8. The permission predicate, repeated at three check points.** *Rule.* Every web-originated harm call (M17 RUPTURE, M17 GOUGE, `apply_suit_damage`) is made only if `exogenous_permitted(section)` holds **at the call tick**, where for a bodily hit `section` is Body's `actor_section(seat)` (crew-body scope, AT-15 R15; not the Graph's `section_of`) and for a hull deposit it is the section of the hull segment. The three check points are: (1) **REACH begin** (HE-14 condition c), (2) **STRIKE entry** (HE-15), (3) **every M17 RUPTURE or GOUGE call** (HE-16, HE-29). **CHILL is a non-harm footprint, permitted in any phase, bounded by HE-F4 and HE-31** (C-HE-28). A REACH may *begin* only in BREACH (not SUBSIDING); an in-flight REACH resolves only if the predicate still holds at its last tick, otherwise it fizzles with no harm, no hairlines, no GOUGE or RUPTURE (a touch-down smear already laid at the hold stage stays: it is true; a fizzle before the hold stage lays none) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Horror issues no STRESS (Attention's alone, AT-11). The registered formula `tell_window_contract` is the audit: for every harm event `e` there is an epoch `k` with `tell_start_k + tell_len_k <= t_e < subside_end_k`, `tell_len_k >= TELL_MIN_TICKS` and `section_e` in `locus_body_k` (the epoch's locus body in force at `t_e`: recorded at TELL entry, replaced only by an AT-14 fallback that TellAudit records as LOCUS_FALLBACK); zero violations over a replay. This GDD **repeats** AT-15; it does not restate a different rule. *Cites.* AT:211, REG `tell_window_contract`, AT:794-810.
153	
154	**HE-9. Tell composition: additive layers, never a substitute.** *Rule.* The Graph's 10-30 s requirement (LSG:144, LSG:1063) is met by **Attention's window** (AT-15); nothing in Horror shortens it, defers it or replaces it. Horror adds layers on top, and a harm path that skips one of them is a defect:
155	
156	| Layer | Owner | Duration | What the player can perceive | Present for |
157	|---|---|---|---|---|
158	| L0 Attention tell | Attention | `TELL_MIN_TICKS` 600 to `TELL_MAX_TICKS` 1800 | beats, filaments, dust, lamp gutter, audio (Attention's) | every harm path |
159	| L1 Presence and stalk | Horror | from ingress (at least `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` after TELL entry) or from TELL entry if already resident, to the first REACH | the entity in light, marks, disturbance dips, audio facts | bodily and hull paths |
160	| L2 REACH telegraph | Horror | `UNFOLD_TICKS` per strike, 95 to 180 ticks | the limb entering the cone before the body, tip resting on the locked point | every strike |
161	| L3 Footprint trail | Horror | continuous, any phase | smear, rime, hairlines | all |
162	| L4 Hull "scrape" | Horror | at least `min_gap` (> `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS`, HE-F15) before a RUPTURE, because the RUPTURE needs the segment in `gouged_seg_ids` from an earlier strike *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | a GOUGE with radial hairlines on the same segment (HE-16) | RUPTURE only |
163	
164	The kernel's illustrative `rng_int(600, 1800)` on the stream name `"horror.tell"` (KRN D.10) is **not** Horror's tell length and not Horror's REACH range; the stream `"attention.tell"` is Attention's. A real horror is a true SIM entity that touches nothing optical.** *Rule.* A horror has a true integer position in its own block, is solid to Layout solids and to nothing else (it passes through crewmates and they through it, BDY-17), is drawn in the single Y-sorted layer so its sprite hides what stands behind it, is hidden by walls and by darkness, and is revealed only by light. It **contributes no occluder, casts no shadow, emits nothing, and never changes the beam, any subject's `lux`, `lit` or any emitter field.** "Real occlusion" in the index row and the routed thread is read as *visual opacity by draw order plus locomotion against Layout solids*, never as a `LightOccluder2D`. Nothing a horror does is a light event except the disturbance state of HE-35, which Lighting reads and executes. *Why.* Three designed GDDs decide it (EM-20 (c) and AC-24; Lighting rail 10 "Horrors cast no shadow and emit nothing" and AC-LO-16; Failure & Trail FT-31) and the art bible's own recommendation agrees (ART:296); a horror shadow would destroy the free stage-2 sanity falsifier "a shadow with no occluder" and with it Pillar 4's "no lie is unfalsifiable". "Displace dust" from the art bible is retained in spirit through the marks of HE-30, not through the Attention Presenter's shared dust process. *(orchestrator ruling: option A, affirmed by the creative-director at the CD-GDD-ALIGN gate as R1; the fiction gloss "the web does not stop light; it only takes it" is adopted; the wording refreshes are owed rows, never edits here.)* **Gate.** Until the owed ART:542, ART 5.5, PIPE:140 and IDX:35 refresh rows land, the art bible and this GDD contradict each other; those rows are a BLOCKING precondition of `/asset-spec` for the rig (AC-HE-123), as C-HE-21 is for rime. *Cites.* EM:208, LO:151, FT:199, ART:296, ART:542.

**HE-3. Block and hook identity.** *Rule.* Block `horror.state`: class `SIM`, `persist` true, `persist_scope` WORLD, scope SHARED, `repl_hint` SHARED_SUMMARY, `schema_version` 1, `supported_versions` [1], `restore_after` `[layout.state, graph.state, emitter.state, attention.state]`. Hook `horror.step`: divisor 5, offset 0, `after: [attention.step, emitter.place]` (the must-repeats of Attention (AT:373), the Emitter (EM AC-60) and the kernel (KRN:201), exactly as ruled; C-HE-20 closed). A hook id that is unknown at boot fails boot (CR-3, no alias concept); grep of `horror.step`, `horror.state` and `horror.view` across the neighbours before closing found no collision. The read view is `horror.view` (HE-37). *Why.* `body.integrate` precedes `horror.step` on every Horror tick through `emitter.place`'s own `after` list (EM:104: `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]`) and the CR-3 total order, so the same-tick seat read that the exact walk-out arithmetic of HE-F2 needs holds without extending the ruled list; Horror writes nothing Body reads, so no cycle can form. A one-tick-stale seat read would let an escaping seat read up to 2 px closer than it is. *Cites.* KRN:71, KRN:201, EM:104, AT:125-131, BDY-8.

**HE-4. Cadence: one run is one rig pose, and what Horror reads between Attention's runs.** *Rule.* `horror.step` runs on ticks that are multiples of 5 (12 Hz), so one run is exactly one 12 fps rig pose (PIPE row 14). Attention and the Graph run at divisor 6; LCM(5, 6) = 30, so the two hooks coincide only when `T mod 30 = 0`, and CR-3's `after` orders the pair only on those ticks. On every other run Horror reads `attention.view` **as committed by Attention's most recent run**; this is a reading of committed state, not a new kernel rule. Presentation interpolates `pos_prev` to `pos_curr` across the five ticks of a run; the rig pose is stepped, never tweened. Every Horror duration is authored as an integer count of runs and published in ticks as `runs × 5` (`HORROR_RUN_TICKS` 5, DERIVED from the divisor); a duration that is not a multiple of 5 is a data-load lint failure (it would silently round up to the next run, a 1 to 4 tick bias that matters at the `UNFOLD_LO` bound). **The lint covers every SIM-clock duration** (`UNFOLD_LO`, `UNFOLD_HI`, `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS`, `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS`, `RETURN_DELAY_TICKS`, `LURK_DWELL_TICKS` and the rest of the type row); it **exempts the L3 disturbance lengths `L3_DUR_LO` and `L3_DUR_HI`** (18 and 30), which are published to Lighting in ticks and are presentation-timed (LO-19, the gutter grammar), not run-quantised: a disturbance *starts* on a run, its length does not round to one (C-HE-29). *Cites.* PIPE:303, KRN:71, HE-F5.

**HE-5. Data-driven type row.** *Rule.* Every per-type value lives in a data file keyed by `type_id`; behaviour code is generic over the row and contains no behavioural constant. A row carries: `v_creep_mpx`, `v_hunt_mpx`, `r_snap_px`, `reach_range_px`, `hull_contact_px`, `strike_bp`, `strike_cooldown_ticks`, `strike_hold_runs`, `unfold_lo`, `unfold_hi`, `lurk_standoff_px`, `lurk_dwell_ticks`, the L3 constants, the mark and rig asset ids. The data lint refuses any field named `damage`, `accuracy`, `armour`, `dps`, `xp`, `unlock`, `health`, `hp`, `kill`, `loot`, `threat`, `aggro` or `hate` (Horror's own harm field is `strike_bp`, a Suit-scale amount, never `damage`). *Why.* Coding standards (gameplay values are data-driven) and the Item DB's lint AP-2; the field list is also the anti-combat guard (HE-38). *Cites.* IDB:97.

**HE-6. Boundaries.** *Rule.* Horror does not read or write Attention's level, does not call `set_beacon`, does not schedule a breach, does not add a Graph footprint kind, does not read any `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, does not move, push or stagger a player (the stagger is the Controller's response to the Suit rung), places no content, narrates nothing, calls no physics query, owns no sound, mix or cue name, owns no HUD element, and holds no stimulus tracker, accumulator, "awareness", "alert", "threat" or "aggro" value, persisted or derived. *Why.* Guard rail 1: absorbing Attention is the most likely way this GDD drifts; the grep of this document for those words outside a negation returns zero (Acceptance Criteria lint).

#### Group B — Permission, tell composition and the audit

**HE-7. Phase-sourced behaviour, no stored drive.** *Rule.* Every transition between LURK and STALK, and every harm gate, is a function of `attention.view` fields only: `phase`, `tell_epoch`, `tell_outcome`, `locus_section_id`, `exogenous_permitted(section)`, `breach_enter_T`, `phase_enter_T`. The target (HE-13) is recomputed from physical `lux` on every run and is **not persisted**. The only things the record remembers are where it is, what state it is in since when, what it has already done this `tell_epoch` (counts), the locked point of a REACH in flight, and the stream counter. **Debug surface** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: a lethal AI cannot be playtested blind)*: each run also publishes a **non-persisted, non-hashed record `horror.view.debug`** on Horror's registered diagnostics channel (Debug Overlay DO-12, dev builds only), holding the current target ref or ANCHOR with each candidate's `lux_pm`, the goal room and the surrogate goal, the next hop, the transition guard that fired (1 to 7) and the HE-14 condition (a) to (f) that failed last, `hold_runs`, `blocked_runs`, `horror_wedged`, and the `linked` and `connected` results for the nearest seat *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. It is derived from the run, never read back: **no SIM rule, guard, formula or hash input may read `horror.view.debug`** (a lint, AC-HE-135), it is absent from `horror.state`, and it is never an accessibility or player surface (UI Requirements). *Why.* AT-2 (one level for the world), Pillar 1 (no hidden stat), guard rail 1. *Cites.* AT:139, AT:214-232.

**HE-8. The permission predicate, repeated at three check points.** *Rule.* Every web-originated harm call (M17 RUPTURE, M17 GOUGE, `apply_suit_damage`) is made only if `exogenous_permitted(section)` holds **at the call tick**, where for a bodily hit `section` is Body's `actor_section(seat)` (crew-body scope, AT-15 R15; not the Graph's `section_of`) and for a hull deposit it is the section of the hull segment. The three check points are: (1) **REACH begin** (HE-14 condition c), (2) **STRIKE entry** (HE-15), (3) **every M17 RUPTURE or GOUGE call** (HE-16, HE-29). **CHILL is a non-harm footprint, permitted in any phase, bounded by HE-F4 and HE-31** (C-HE-28). A REACH may *begin* only in BREACH (not SUBSIDING); an in-flight REACH resolves only if the predicate still holds at its last tick, otherwise it fizzles with no harm, no hairlines, no GOUGE or RUPTURE (a touch-down smear already laid at the hold stage stays: it is true; a fizzle before the hold stage lays none) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Horror issues no STRESS (Attention's alone, AT-11). The registered formula `tell_window_contract` is the audit: for every harm event `e` there is an epoch `k` with `tell_start_k + tell_len_k <= t_e < subside_end_k`, `tell_len_k >= TELL_MIN_TICKS` and `section_e` in `locus_body_k` (the epoch's locus body in force at `t_e`: recorded at TELL entry, replaced only by an AT-14 fallback that TellAudit records as LOCUS_FALLBACK); zero violations over a replay. This GDD **repeats** AT-15; it does not restate a different rule. *Cites.* AT:211, REG `tell_window_contract`, AT:794-810.

**HE-9. Tell composition: additive layers, never a substitute.** *Rule.* The Graph's 10-30 s requirement (LSG:144, LSG:1063) is met by **Attention's window** (AT-15); nothing in Horror shortens it, defers it or replaces it. Horror adds layers on top, and a harm path that skips one of them is a defect:

| Layer | Owner | Duration | What the player can perceive | Present for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L0 Attention tell | Attention | `TELL_MIN_TICKS` 600 to `TELL_MAX_TICKS` 1800 | beats, filaments, dust, lamp gutter, audio (Attention's) | every harm path |
| L1 Presence and stalk | Horror | from ingress (at least `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` after TELL entry) or from TELL entry if already resident, to the first REACH | the entity in light, marks, disturbance dips, audio facts | bodily and hull paths |
| L2 REACH telegraph | Horror | `UNFOLD_TICKS` per strike, 95 to 180 ticks | the limb entering the cone before the body, tip resting on the locked point | every strike |
| L3 Footprint trail | Horror | continuous, any phase | smear, rime, hairlines | all |
| L4 Hull "scrape" | Horror | at least `min_gap` (> `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS`, HE-F15) before a RUPTURE, because the RUPTURE needs the segment in `gouged_seg_ids` from an earlier strike *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | a GOUGE with radial hairlines on the same segment (HE-16) | RUPTURE only |

The kernel's illustrative `rng_int(600, 1800)` on the stream name `"horror.tell"` (KRN D.10) is **not** Horror's tell length and not Horror's REACH range; the stream `"attention.tell"` is Attention's. Horror draws from `"horror.tell"` only the REACH length (HE-14). *Cites.* LSG:144, AT:211, KRN D.10, reflexion entry on examples read as contracts.

170	**HE-11. LURK: the non-lethal CALM presence.** *Rule.* In CALM a resident record is in LURK in its current body. It loiters at `V_CREEP_MPX` between waypoints drawn from Layout `anchor_geometry`: it dwells `LURK_DWELL_TICKS` at a waypoint, then the next waypoint is the lowest-hash candidate (`he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP)`, HE-42; the chosen waypoint is held in the persisted `goal_wp` and the dwell start in `dwell_start_T`, HE-41) among waypoints in loaded sections of its body that are at least `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` from every living seat. It **never starts a move that brings it, or leaves it, nearer than `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` to a living seat** (the invariant is on the horror's own motion: a seat that walks toward it closes the gap itself, and the horror then steps away along the room graph; if cornered it holds still and does nothing). **Every `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` comparison in this rule (the standoff, the step-away and the waypoint filter) applies only to a seat for which `linked(horror, seat)` holds (HE-19)**: a room-level test that does not change while both stand in their rooms, so a horror at a doorway cannot oscillate between the standoff and step-away rules on a jamb graze, and a seat two short rooms away in open line of sight is linked; a seat in an unlinked room behind a wall does not push it away and is not a reason to hold still *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. It deposits no RUPTURE and no GOUGE and applies no suit damage; it may be seen, lays marks (HE-30), makes CHILL deposits (HE-27) and disturbance dips (HE-35). A seat may walk through it (no collision, BDY-17); that costs nothing and is a free moment of inspection. Its transitions out of LURK come **only from `attention.view.phase`**, never from the player's light, noise or distance. *Why.* Attention's "CALM is never known-safe" (AT:92, AT:373) is a claim about the phase (a TELL can begin at any time), not a claim that this presence can hurt, and this rule does not imply one: the CALM presence is provably harmless (no harm call, the standoff, the step-away) and **what a CALM sighting is worth is information**: which body it lives in (`RETURN_HOME`), and that its trail and rime are fresh (stage-0 marks), so the player may change the route, the lamp or the first job. It is not made dangerous to keep the dread up, because a harm in CALM would arrive with no tell and break Pillar 2; the standoff and the phase-only transitions also keep it from becoming a timer or a second meter (AT-2). Validation target (7) measures whether the information is used (AC-HE-122); if it is not, the first lever is `RETURN_HOME` 0 (OQ-1), never relaxing this rule. *Cites.* AT:92, AT:373.

172	**HE-12. STALK: creep in a TELL, hunt in a BREACH.** *Rule.* On a TELL entry (a `tell_epoch` different from the record's `last_seen_tell_epoch`; **this comparison is the first evaluation for every record in every run, ahead of the dormancy guard**, States and Transitions guard 2) a record whose body holds the locus goes LURK → STALK; a record in another body goes LURK → TRANSIT (HE-20), **even when its own body is unloaded** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. In a TELL, STALK moves toward the target (HE-13) at `V_CREEP_MPX` and stops at `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` from every living seat that is `linked` to it (HE-19) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; it deposits no RUPTURE and no GOUGE and calls no `apply_suit_damage`. In BREACH it moves at `V_HUNT_MPX` and closes to `REACH_RANGE_PX` of the target point. STALK is one state; the speed is a function of `attention.view.phase`. **A TELL abort** (the phase leaves TELL with an aborted `tell_outcome`) returns STALK to LURK with no strike and no mark burst, and **cancels an outbound TRANSIT** (HE-20) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Entering SUBSIDING sends STALK to RETREAT. *Why.* Pillar 2 (the stalk is the additive earlier layer) and Pillar 3. *Cites.* AT:373, AT-16.

174	**HE-13. Target from physical light.** *Rule.* Candidates are living seats (not DOWNED, DEAD or IN_POD per the Controller's `loco_state`) whose `actor_section` is in `locus_body` (TELL, BREACH, SUBSIDING) or in the record's own body (CALM). One `lux(ref)` read per candidate per run, zero probes. **The target rule, stated plainly** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a candidate is *lit* when its total light `lux_pm(s) >= LIT_ON_PM` (150, CITED), a stateless comparison on the same quantity the argmax uses (the comparison is made fresh every run and nothing is stored; there is no off-threshold and no hysteresis, as for the Emitter's `probe` `lit_on`). **Horror does not gate on the Emitter's `lit` bit**: that bit is a hysteresis on `act_lux_pm`, which excludes the owner's own beam (EM-2, EM-21, EM AC-16a), so a lone player in the dark with the lamp on reads `lux_pm` 1000 but `act_lux_pm` 0 and would never be a candidate; the Emitter's own wording ("Horror sees a lit player", EM line 685) is the contract. Any light that raises `lux_pm` counts, including a fixture (the self-powered status glow of a docked pod's dock-room prop is an ordinary lit fixture by user ruling X2, so a seat at the dock console is a lit candidate and Horror adds no exception for it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*), a node lantern, a Chemlight pool, another crewmate's beam and the BEACON's sweep (the BEACON does not gate actions but does count in `lux_pm`; a seat swept by it is lit for as long as `lux_pm` stays at or above the threshold, and because P locks at REACH start a flapping lit state cannot steer a strike). **A seat standing in fixture light is lit and can be targeted with its own lamp off**; going dark means leaving the light, not only switching the lamp off (HE-26). The target is the lit candidate with the highest `lux_pm`, ties lowest seat id. **The argmax is therefore degenerate among seats whose own lamp is on**: each reads 1000 (the owner stands in their own light, EM-21), so the lowest seat id wins; the argmax discriminates only among seats lit by *other* light (fixtures, pools, a teammate's beam), and it is the presence of light, not its amount, that draws the horror. If no candidate is lit, the target is the locus section's anchor (the anchor REACH of HE-16). **The preference is recomputed every run and never stored.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The *walk* it leads to is committed, the target is not: the chosen goal waypoint is held in the persisted `goal_wp` for `GOAL_COMMIT_RUNS` runs (12, 60 ticks) unless it is reached, its seat leaves the candidate set, the phase changes, the layout changes or the goal becomes unreachable, so a lone seat on a lux boundary or under an L3 dip cannot make the stalk dither at 12 Hz (the layer players read as "it was hunting me"); REACH begin (HE-14) always reads the fresh target. The horror moves identically lit or unlit and is never repelled, stunned, slowed or harmed by light. This GDD **adopts the Emitter's text verbatim**, as the second GDD to land: "No beam stuns, burns, repels or damages a horror or a crewmate ... being revealed is the beam's whole effect" (EM:89). Objects are never targets at MVP: a dropped glowstick is a Chemlight pool that counts as exposure to whoever stands in it, but it is not a seat, so it does not pull the horror toward itself; flares, torches and decoys that repel or distract are Vertical Slice (EM:89). *Why.* Pillar 3 made legible ("you lit up, it came") with no meter. With two or more lit seats a stateless argmax can alternate; a hysteresis would need a stored value, which is a Vertical Slice question (Open Questions). *Cites.* EM:89, EM-21.

178	**HE-15. A seat standing on a door sill belongs to the sill's room (Layout `room_at`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The strike's wall test is the **strict same-room clause only**: the second branch of `connected` (an adjacent room across an open, passable sill, HE-19) applies to REACH begin and nowhere in the strike, so a seat in the adjacent room across an open sill is spared even though a REACH could begin toward it (AC-HE-27). Breadth-first by hop count, ties lowest room id, at most `PATH_EXPANSIONS_MAX` node expansions per run (HE-F10); the result is cached as a next-hop table per goal room and layout key. **One graph, one goal rule (the surrogate-goal BFS)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the text had defined the pathing graph two ways, an open-leaf BFS and the full adjacency truncated at a closed leaf)*: the goal room is chosen over the full adjacency (closed and impassable leaves counted for distance, E-HE-20); the search runs on the passable-leaf graph only; when the goal room is not reachable the *surrogate goal* is the reachable room with the smallest full-adjacency hop distance to the goal room (ties lowest room id), and the horror walks there and stops. Inside a room it steers by octant toward the next waypoint (the centre of a door's hinge-aware `gap_rect`, not the sill centre or the leaf, or an `anchor_geometry` point) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a waypoint is **reached** when the foot point is within `ARRIVE_PX` (8 px [PH], at least the largest per-run displacement, 8 px at `V_HUNT_MPX`, so a run can never step over a waypoint) of it. There is no obstacle avoidance beyond the **local slide rule**, which uses only the persisted `blocked_runs` counter: when the previous run ended `blocked`, `blocked_runs` is 1 and the run uses the adjacent octant (±1) with the larger dot product against the direction to the waypoint (ties lowest octant); at `blocked_runs` 2 it uses the other adjacent octant; from 3 it returns to the direct octant. Authoring contract: a room's walkable floor must let straight octant steps between its sills and anchors succeed with at most this slide (lint `ROOM_NONCONVEX_PATH`, owed to Layout and Derelict Authoring; an L-shaped footprint fixture is AC-HE-128). On a NONE or UNKNOWN Layout read it holds its last waypoint for at most `HOLD_MAX_RUNS` (counted in the persisted `hold_runs`), and then **the fallback depends on the phase: in CALM and TELL it goes to LURK; in BREACH it stays in STALK and holds position (LURK is n/a in BREACH, so a hold-then-LURK there would break the phase view and leave a breach with a horror that cannot do harm); in SUBSIDING it goes to RETREAT**; a record in RETREAT holds in place in any phase *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; **UNKNOWN is never read as "unlit" or as "open"**. If `step` reports no movement for `BLOCKED_RUNS_MAX` consecutive runs it discards the cached hop and re-paths once; if it is still without movement after a second `BLOCKED_RUNS_MAX` runs it is **wedged**, and the defined outcome is RETREAT (counter `horror_wedged`, `cooldown_until_T := T`; in BREACH it then returns to STALK and re-paths, so a wedge repeats visibly in the diagnostics and is an authoring signal, never a silent permanent stall) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Zero `probe()` calls at MVP. `NavigationServer2D` and `NavigationAgent2D` are rejected (node- and server-based, outside the replay hash; H10, G3). `route_length_px` stays diagnostic (LY:310). Layout now states (ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md, LY-28 reads and LY-33) that `layout_hash()` does **not** cover door state and that a reader caching on door geometry keys on `version(section_id)`; the cache key is therefore `(goal_room, layout_hash, version(section_id) of every section of the body)`, a restore (where `version` resets) is an unconditional rebuild, and the Horror-computed closed-leaf hash is retired (C-HE-13 closed 2026-10-27, design review). -> ADR candidate (2). *Cites.* LY:296-310, LY:446, EM:723.
203	
204	**HE-26. Doors and the counterplay set.** *Rule.* A closed door leaf is solid to the horror (Layout `solid_in`). It issues no `set_opening`, opens no door, and may GOUGE or RUPTURE a hull segment, never a door. The **whole MVP counterplay set** is: retreat (walk away: `V_HUNT_MPX < V_WALK × 1000`), close a door (the strike room test and solid leaf; the horror holds at the sill and marks the leaf, below), go dark (the seat leaves target preference on the next run **only if no other light reaches it: a lamp-off seat under a lit fixture or in a Chemlight pool is still lit and still targetable, HE-13** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; its price is every lit-only channelled verb for the breach and the ship under STRESS unattended), pod-hop (the departed seat leaves `locus_body`, so `exogenous_permitted(actor_section(seat))` fails and an in-flight REACH on it fizzles; on a derelict locus, the departure of the last occupant recorded at BREACH entry also ends the breach, AT-12 (iii)), drop the cargo (turns a carrier into a walker) and the **glowstick work-light** (*light the job, not yourself*: a thrown Chemlight lights a workspace so the player can step out of it dark; it does not pull the horror). The suppressant is *not* in the set (HE-39). **A horror may path and stand in derelict A's `a_spine` at the MVP** (Boarding ASK-BS-H1 / OQ-BS-33 answered by the owner) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R21: the option that needs the least new content and preserves user rulings X6 and D63)*: ingress (HE-20) lands at a hull entry one room hop from the lit seat's room and never in a living seat's room, and a stalking horror follows the lit seat through any open door, so a carrier in the 3-wide spine can meet one. No bypass is added and the spine is not widened, because the ruled exits already hold in a single corridor: drop the cargo and walk back the way the carrier came (a walking seat outpaces `V_HUNT_MPX`, HE-24), stillness and darkness, or a door shut behind; this is the intended price of hauling (D63, 7 of 18 draws for a carrier who keeps the cargo, E-HE-27). The existing guards are the dead-end lint (E-HE-26) and the drop's one-free-cell question (Open Question 7); E-HE-59. **The anti-pillar's "tools may repel or distract (flares, torches, decoys)" is deliberately unused at MVP and deferred to Vertical Slice (`repel`, flares, decoys): MVP counterplay is avoidance only, and the routed thread's "tools repel, never kill" is a boundary (no tool ever kills, HE-38) and not an MVP promise that a tool repels.** *(orchestrator ruling: the earlier phrase "glowstick lure" is reworded because HE-13 prefers seats only and a glowstick is not a seat; creative-director concurs; decoys are Vertical Slice.)* No response is free and none is dominant: abort loses the job, hiding loses the task and the ship, going dark loses the lit verbs, committing risks a rung. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)* **A closed door is a priced, visible refuge** (the creative-director's lean, taken because the user delegated the call). When the target is a lit seat behind a closed or impassable leaf, the horror walks to the surrogate goal (HE-25) and **camps at the sill**: on the run it becomes stationary there (edge-triggered by the persisted `held_at_leaf` flag) it lays one HAIRLINES mark on the leaf face (a true ring entry; no M17 call, no hull damage, no GOUGE, no RUPTURE; counter `horror_leaf_marks`), and it stays while that seat remains the target and the phase is BREACH, recomputing the target every run as ever. The door therefore costs what the rules already price (the task, the ship under STRESS, the lit verbs while dark) and now also shows the player that the thing is waiting on the other side, with the leaf mark as the post-hoc evidence; what it does not do is damage the ship on the player's behalf. The alternatives (an anchor GOUGE fallback; leaving the playtest band as the only price) are recorded in Open Question 33 and not adopted. **A door closed on the horror.** If a leaf closes while the horror's foot box overlaps it (Layout's close-safety counts seats' foot boxes, not the horror's), the next run ejects it as the first step of guard 4: it moves back along `−last_octant` in 8 px increments up to 32 px to the first position for which `solid_in(foot_box)` is false (at most four queries, inside the five-query budget); if none is free it is wedged (RETREAT, `horror_wedged`, HE-25). It never embeds, wedges silently or passes through a leaf; counter `horror_door_ejected`; AC-HE-137. The preferred long-term fix, Layout's close-safety including a published horror foot box (`OBSTRUCTED`), is an ask in Open Question 32 and would make the eject unreachable. *Cites.* AT-12, DA-29, EM:89.
